learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding of general, organic and inorganic chemistry underlying the industrial engineering branch.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve problems in general, organic and inorganic chemistry using established methods.
Be able to design and conduct chemistry experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Have technical and laboratory chemistry competences.
Be able to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods to solve problems in general, organic and inorganic chemistry.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve problems in general, organic and inorganic chemistry.
Function effectively both individually and in a team.
Knowledge and understanding of the scientific and mathematical principles underlying their branch of engineering.
Ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
Ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
Ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Electromagnetic radiation. Wave-particle duality. Bohr atomic model. Concept of probability. Schrödinger approximation.
Atomic orbitals. Energy of orbitals. Filling order of atomic orbitals. Exceptions to the filling rule. Electronic configuration in monatomic ions.
Periodic properties. Atomic radii. Ionic radius. Ionization energy. Electron affinity. Electronegativity.
The Ionic bond. Crystal structure. Properties of Ionic Compounds.
The Covalent Bond. Ionic Character of the Covalent Bond. Molecular polarity. Valence bond theory. Hybridization.
The Metallic bond. Structure of the metallic bond.
Gases. Kinetic theory of gases. Mixtures of Ideal Gases.
Changes of state. Liquid-vapor equilibrium. Variation of vapor pressure with temperature. Clausius equation. Clausius-Clapeyron equation.
Solubility. Factors influencing solubility. Solubility of gases. Henry's Law. Distribution law.
Ideal gas solution. Raoult's Law. Deviations from Raoult's Law.
Boiling point diagrams. Distillation. Freezing point diagrams.
Colligative properties. Decrease in vapor pressure. Increase in boiling temperature. Decrease in melting/freezing temperature. Osmotic pressure.
Definition of Thermochemistry and Types of Systems.
Indirect determination of reaction enthalpies: Hess's Law.
The first law of thermodynamics: Heat, Work and Enthalpy.
The second law of Thermodynamics: Entropy and disorder, Spontaneity, reversibility and equilibrium.
Acid-base definitions. Arrhenius theory. Brønsted-Lowry theory. Lewis theory.
Acid-base properties of water. Acidic, basic and neutral solutions.
Strength of acids and bases. Relationship between acidity constant and basicity constant.
Solubility. Solubility product. Precipitation reactions. Common ion effect on solubility.
Applications of Electrolytic Cells. Faraday's Law.
Corrosion Cells. Cathodic protection and passivation.
Concept and fundamentals of Chemical Engineering.
Identification of organic compound families. Nomenclature of organic compounds.
Hydrocarbons. Description of bonding in saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons. Nomenclature and formulation of hydrocarbons. Physical properties of aliphatic hydrocarbons.
Types of organic reactions. Reaction intermediates: radical, carbocation and carbanion. Aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbons.
Main sources of hydrocarbons: petroleum, natural gas and coal.
Petroleum processing. Industrial use of fossil fuels.
Alcohols, phenols and ethers. Properties, preparation methods. Applications.

assessment_methods.method: Participation and report submission for laboratory practice sessions

assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation accounts for 40% of the grade, comprising three tests (15% for topics 1-6 and 15% for topics 6-11) and participation/lab reports (10%). The final exam accounts for 60% of the grade, with a minimum required score of 4. Completion of laboratory practices is mandatory for evaluation.
